subject: Clarify delete-request eligibility, archived snapshots, and KMS handling
messages:
From: Sara Li <sara.li@finova.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Alex Torres <alex.torres@finova.com>
Date: 2026-08-01T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Next steps on deletion requirements and retention

Hi Karthik —

Thanks for the call earlier. A quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions so legal and privacy ops can sign off: 

1) Scope: We need confirmation that customer-initiated RTBF/delete requests will remove PII from (a) the live model serving dataset, (b) any inference logs, and (c) longer-term backups/snapshots.
2) Backups: What is the timeline to remove data from encrypted backups and any snapshot retention windows (including immutable snapshots)?
3) KMS: If we bring our own KMS for keys, will Redwood still be able to purge associated encrypted blobs upon request?
4) Evidence: Our auditor will want a high-level playbook and a simple evidence template showing steps and timelines.

Can you confirm who on your side will own the technical steps vs. the legal notification? Also, please attach any short playbook you can share.

Appreciate it — we’re trying to finalize the data handling section of our vendor assessment by Friday.

— Sara Li
Senior Privacy Counsel
Finova Payments
[Attachment: finova-delete-scenarios.xlsx]

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Sara Li <sara.li@finova.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-02T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps on deletion requirements and retention

Hi Sara —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, followed by recommended next steps: 

- Live serving + logs: We can remove the customer’s PII from the live serving layer and inference logs within the SLA window (standard: 72 hours after request acceptance). Logs that have been exported to external systems (e.g., customer SIEM) are not under our control unless previously arranged.

- Backups & snapshots: We keep rolling snapshots for disaster recovery. Typical retention window is 30 days for fast snapshots, and quarterly archival snapshots for up to 12 months depending on plan. For delete requests we support two paths: 
  • Standard purge: overwrite selectable ranges in the active dataset and delete associated KV caches; archival snapshots remain until retention expires (we mark affected snapshots for redaction where possible).
  • Escalated purge: for enterprise customers (and with an approved contract amendment) we can trigger a targeted archive overwrite and accelerate snapshot expiry where the environment is in our managed storage (timeline usually 7–30 days depending on storage provider and immutable snapshot policy).

- KMS: If you use BYOK/KMS and keys are customer-controlled, we can remove object references and zero out metadata; however, physical ciphertext may remain in storage if we cannot re-encrypt or rewrap without the customer key. In practice teams mitigate by revoking keys and coordinating a separate archival purge. We’ll need legal confirmation on the acceptable proof-of-deletion artifact in BYOK cases.

- Evidence: Attached is a concise playbook and a SOC2-style evidence request template that legal often finds useful.

Requested next steps: 
1) Can you confirm whether Finova will use BYOK for this integration? (yes/no)
2) If BYOK = yes, can you share the KMS model and whether the key will be hosted in your cloud account?
3) Do you expect requests to include deletion of embeddings or only original user content?

I’ve attached the playbook and the evidence template. If it helps, Marissa is available for a short technical-runbook session this week.

Thanks,
Karthik
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-delete-playbook.pdf]
[Attachment: SOC2-evidence-request-template.xlsx]

From: Sara Li <sara.li@finova.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Alex Torres <alex.torres@finova.com>
Date: 2026-08-02T13:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps on deletion requirements and retention

Karthik —

Answers below so we can move forward: 

1) BYOK: Yes — Finova intends to use our existing KMS in AWS (key stored in our account, not shared).
2) Embeddings: We consider embeddings derived from PII to fall under the same request scope; deletion must remove model-side embeddings and any cached representations.
3) Timeline expectation: Legal can accept the standard 72-hour purge for live + logs. For backups/archives we need an accelerated option in 30 days or fewer; can you confirm Redwood can commit to that in an enterprise addendum?

Also attaching our scenarios spreadsheet — there are two high-priority customers there (rows highlighted). Please confirm whether an accelerated purge action would require a maintenance window that impacts availability.

Thanks,
Sara
[Attachment: finova-delete-scenarios.xlsx]

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-03T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Next steps on deletion requirements and retention (internal)

Internal note / action items — forwarding Sara's answers and the attached Finova scenarios. Two immediate asks: 

1) Contract amendment: Legal will want wording for an "Accelerated Archive Purge" (target: 30 days) and a clear definition of what we can guarantee under BYOK. Marissa — can you draft a short clause and estimated SOW-level pricing for RD team review?

2) Technical feasibility: Dev — can you confirm for managed storage (S3 / Azure Blob) whether we can perform an archive-targeted overwrite and what the dependent windows are for immutable snapshots? Specifically call out: immutable snapshot retention, provider snapshot reconciliation time, and any replication lag that could keep ciphertext around beyond 30 days. Also indicate whether we need a planned maintenance window for accelerating purge.

Cc-ing the attachments in the thread for reference. I’ll propose a 30-minute sync with Finova after we have the contract wording and a short tech note.

Thanks — Karthik
